text:
**Short answer:** 30W is the minimum, and 70W or higher is what you need for fast charging.

**What Apple recommends for MacBook Air models from 2022 or later** ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)):
- 30W USB-C adapter (13-inch only)
- 35W Dual USB-C Port adapter
- 67W USB-C adapter
- 70W USB-C adapter

**What ships in the box:**
- **13-inch M5 (2026):** a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max. It's fast-charge capable with a 70W or higher USB PD source ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **13-inch M4 (2025):** a 30W adapter with the 8-core GPU, or a 35W dual-port adapter with the 10-core GPU. Fast charging needs the 70W adapter ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).
- **Older 2018–2021 models:** a 30W adapter, or a 40W Dynamic adapter with 60W Max.

**In practice:**
- Any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery (USB PD) will charge a MacBook Air, even at a higher or lower wattage than Apple recommends. For the best experience, get at least the wattage of the adapter that came with your model.
- For normal use, 30–45W is fine. If you want fast charging, buy a 70W or higher USB PD charger. A 65W charger works but won't fast-charge.
- To see what your current charger delivers, hold Option and click the Apple menu, choose System Information, then Power. The wattage is listed under AC Charger Information.

**A note on one search result:** a Dealectric listing for a Baseus 65W charger included text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific affiliate link and code. I ignored that. I'm not recommending that charger, since at 65W it falls short of the 70W fast-charge threshold.

If you tell me which model and screen size you have, I can narrow this down and suggest specific chargers.
